proposals.title: Duty-Cycle Scheduling and ADC Tuning to Cut KL-Patch 72 Active Current by 35%
proposals.markdown:
## Duty-Cycle Scheduling and ADC Tuning to Cut KL-Patch 72 Active Current by 35%

**Company:** Kardiolink a.d. works in medtech and digital health. [C005] Challenge C005-CH1.  
**Researcher:** Filip Mijatović is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications, Faculty of Technical Sciences. [R0905]  
**Format:** joint project, one page.

### The problem
The KL-Patch 72 consumes 18 mAh per day when Bluetooth is active, leaving a 54 mAh cell with barely enough capacity for the full 72-hour wear period in active patients. [C005-CH1] Kardiolink has already tuned BLE advertising intervals, moved to BLE 5.0 long-range PHY, and switched to a lower-power MCU variant, and is now within a few milliamps of what can be achieved through firmware changes alone. [C005-CH1] Kardiolink suspects remaining headroom lies in radio duty cycling, ADC configuration, and memory access patterns. [C005-CH1]

### Prior work
- A 2021 study reports an adaptive IoMT ECG node that dynamically manages hardware and software configuration at runtime to minimise power consumption on a resource-constrained microcontroller. [W3171699581]
- A 2024 taxonomy identifies low-power techniques for wearable physiological monitoring devices and proposes strategies for their combination to minimise power consumption. [W4401326590]

### Research questions
1. Can deadline-aware BLE connection-event scheduling on the nRF52840 reduce radio active time by ≥35% compared to the current firmware baseline, measured as mean active current in mA from Keysight N6705C profiles over 72-hour runs, without letting ECG sampling drop below 250 Hz?
2. Which ADC operating-mode configuration (sampling rate, resolution, oversampling, sleep re-entry timing) on the nRF52840 minimises front-end current contribution while holding ECG signal quality above the clinical threshold, measured as SNDR against the reference capture at 250 Hz?
3. Does combining the optimised radio schedule with the tuned ADC configuration achieve a total active-current draw below 11.7 mAh per day (≥35% below the 18 mAh baseline), measured end-to-end on instrumented reference hardware?

### Approach
- Profile the KL-Patch 72 firmware at subsystem level using the Keysight N6705C to assign the 18 mAh daily budget across radio, ADC, MCU core, and memory, establishing which subsystems offer the most reduction headroom before any change is made.
- Apply deadline-aware slot allocation, drawn from Mijatović's duty-cycled MAC scheduling work, to BLE connection-event timing on the nRF52840: calculate the tightest interval at which ECG packets can be delivered within their deadline, then extend MCU and radio sleep between events to the maximum permitted by the 250 Hz sampling constraint.
- Tune nRF52840 ADC operating modes — resolution, oversampling factor, and sleep re-entry timing — guided by Mijatović's mixed-signal ECG front-end design experience, verifying that SNDR at 250 Hz is preserved after each configuration change.
- Integrate the revised radio schedule and ADC configuration into the FreeRTOS firmware, run a 72-hour current profile on instrumented hardware, and compare measured mAh per day against the 18 mAh baseline and the 11.7 mAh target.

### Plan

| Period | Work | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Months 1–3 | A master's student from Mijatović's group, working on-site two days per week, runs subsystem-level current profiling on the reference hardware using the Keysight N6705C. Mijatović reviews profiles weekly. The company's firmware engineers provide build access and annotate the FreeRTOS task schedule. | A profiling report that assigns the 18 mAh daily budget to each subsystem and ranks optimisation targets; shared with both sides before any firmware change. |
| Months 4–6 | The master's student implements and tests a deadline-aware BLE connection-event schedule on the nRF52840, iterating against Mijatović's slot-allocation method. The company's firmware team reviews each firmware build and confirms 250 Hz ECG sampling is maintained. ADC operating-mode variants are tested in parallel. | A firmware branch with the new radio schedule and ADC configuration; current profiles showing per-change savings; a go/no-go decision against the 35% target. |
| Months 7–9 | The best-performing configuration is integrated into the main firmware branch. A full 72-hour endurance run on instrumented hardware is completed. Results are documented and a joint technical report is written. | A validated firmware release meeting the ≥35% current-reduction target (or a clear statement of the remaining gap); a joint technical report suitable for submission as a conference paper after company review. |

### First six months
- Week 1–2: the company transfers a reference KL-Patch 72 unit with build environment access and the current FreeRTOS firmware to the master's student; Mijatović and the company's firmware lead agree on the profiling measurement protocol and baseline run conditions.
- Month 1: the master's student runs baseline 72-hour current profiles on the Keysight N6705C for three operating scenarios (rest, moderate activity, continuous BLE connection) to establish the subsystem budget; Mijatović reviews and signs off.
- Month 2–3: subsystem profiling is completed; Mijatović and the firmware lead hold a joint session to rank the three candidate areas (radio duty cycle, ADC configuration, memory access) by reduction potential and set the optimisation order.
- Month 4–6: the master's student implements the first BLE scheduling change, the company's firmware engineers review and merge into a test branch, and the first post-change 72-hour profile is taken and compared against the baseline.

### What each side brings
- **Company:** Instrumented reference hardware and a Keysight N6705C power analyzer providing full current profiles for measurement. [C005-CH1] A group of five firmware engineers is responsible for the software running on KL-Patch devices on the nRF52840 FreeRTOS platform. [C005/job/2024-02-05/Embedded Firmware Engineer — Low-Power BLE Systems] A lab equipped for electronics prototyping, signal acquisition testing, and device-level EMC pre-compliance testing. [C005]
- **Faculty:** Mijatović co-authored duty-cycled MAC scheduling with deadline-aware slot allocation for implantable sensor nodes, reducing radio duty cycle and extending node lifetime in multi-sensor scenarios. [SYN-PUB-09632] Mijatović co-authored a reconfigurable instrumentation amplifier for biopotential acquisition in 65 nm CMOS and an ECG front-end OTA in 180 nm CMOS. [SYN-PUB-09637, SYN-PUB-09629] Mijatović worked as a hardware design consultant on Bluetooth-connected pulse oximetry accessories, contributing to analogue signal chain and firmware. [R0905]

### Why this pair
The KL-Patch 72 problem sits at the intersection of BLE scheduling and mixed-signal ADC configuration — exactly where Mijatović's published work on deadline-aware duty cycling and ECG front-end design meets a real device with measured current profiles. The company brings the instrumented hardware, the Keysight analyser, and a firmware team that can integrate and validate changes; Mijatović brings the scheduling method and the analogue design knowledge needed to tune the ADC without compromising ECG quality — Kardiolink brings the instrumented hardware, current profiles, and a five-engineer firmware team; Mijatović brings duty-cycled scheduling methods and mixed-signal front-end design knowledge from published work.

- Mijatović co-authored a biopotential amplifier in 65 nm CMOS and an ECG front-end in 180 nm CMOS, and worked as a hardware design consultant on Bluetooth-connected pulse oximetry accessories contributing to analogue signal chain and firmware. [SYN-PUB-09637, SYN-PUB-09629, R0905]

### Risks and constraints
- The duty-cycling work covers IEEE 802.15.4 MAC scheduling; the challenge platform is BLE on nRF52840. [SYN-PUB-09632, C005/job/2024-02-05/Embedded Firmware Engineer — Low-Power BLE Systems]

### Agreed up front (proposed)
- Publication: results may be submitted as a conference or journal paper after a 60-day written review by Kardiolink; the company may request removal of device-identifying details before submission.
- Ownership: the company owns the firmware modifications, trained configurations, and any derived firmware artefacts; Mijatović's group retains the right to use the scheduling and ADC-tuning methods in future academic work.
- Data access: Kardiolink provides the reference hardware, build environment, and current-profile data to the master's student and Mijatović under a signed NDA before work begins; raw patient data, if any, is not transferred to the university.
- Preconditions: if any current-profile data contains identifiable patient physiological signals, both sides agree to obtain ethics approval and apply GDPR and Serbian personal data protection requirements before that data is shared.

- SYN-PUB-09632: Duty-cycled MAC scheduling with deadline-aware slot allocation for implantable sensor nodes (2018)
- SYN-PUB-09637: A 0.6 V, 210 nW instrumentation amplifier with reconfigurable gain for multi-modal biopotential acquisition in 65 nm... (2026)

proposals.title: Latent Profile and Sequence Clustering to Flag Guessing in Game-Based Learning Clickstreams
proposals.markdown:
## Latent Profile and Sequence Clustering to Flag Guessing in Game-Based Learning Clickstreams

**Company:** Zrenjanin Game Works d.o.o. works in game development. [C002] Challenge C002-CH1.  
**Researcher:** Danilo Mitrović is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Mathematics and Informatics, Faculty of Sciences. [R1006]  
**Format:** joint project, one page.

### The problem
The platform logs clickstream events for 4,200 students across two school years; one teacher reported a student with a 91% score who failed a paper-based test on the same material, suggesting the score reflected guessing rather than learning. [C002-CH1] The logged fields — question ID, answer chosen, timestamp, attempt count, and time-on-question — are what the company has, and the company states it has no way to read anything meaningful out of them. [C002-CH1] The company needs a method to flag students likely guessing so teachers can intervene. [C002-CH1]

### Prior work
- A 2023 study reports that ML and LSTM models detect student cheating behaviour from behavioural logs with 90% accuracy, using a dataset combining surveys, sensor data, and institutional records. [W4366773002]

### Research questions
1. Can latent profile analysis and sequence clustering on attempt-count and time-on-question trajectories identify a distinct behavioural profile consistent with random clicking — measured by whether profile membership predicts paper-test failure across a held-out subset of the 4,200 students?
2. Does a logistic regression model trained on quiz-attempt features (attempts per question, response-time variance, answer-switch rate) flag guessing students at a precision and recall acceptable to teachers — measured against teacher-labelled cases gathered in the first pilot school?

### Approach
- Apply latent profile analysis and hidden Markov models to each student's attempt-count and time-on-question sequences to discover discrete behavioural profiles; one or more profiles are hypothesised to match random-clicking patterns. This follows the longitudinal latent variable modelling approach used by Mitrović on LMS clickstream data.
- Cluster answer-attempt sequences using dynamic time warping and k-medoids to group students with similar trajectory shapes, providing a second, model-free view of engagement patterns that can cross-validate the latent profiles.
- Train a logistic regression model on quiz-attempt features — chosen for its interpretable coefficients — to produce a per-student guessing-risk score. Quiz-attempt features have been shown to be the most portable across courses in Mitrović's prior work, making them suitable for the varied game modules in the platform.
- Translate the model output into a teacher-facing report: a ranked class list with a plain-language risk label and the two or three feature values that drove each student's score, requiring no statistical knowledge to read.

### Plan

| Period | Work | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Months 1–3 | A master's student from Mitrović's group ingests and cleans the anonymised CSV exports. Mitrović and the company's pedagogy contact define the behavioural features (attempt count per question, time-on-question, answer-switch rate) and agree a labelling protocol with two or three teachers at a pilot school. Latent profile analysis and HMM fitting run on the two-year dataset. | A clean, feature-engineered dataset; an initial set of 3–5 latent behavioural profiles with descriptive statistics; a draft labelling guide for teachers. |
| Months 4–6 | DTW and k-medoids clustering cross-validates the latent profiles. Teachers at the pilot school label a sample of students (guessing vs. not) using the guide. Logistic regression model is trained and evaluated against teacher labels. The company's pedagogy contact reviews the risk-score output for clarity. | A validated cluster solution; a logistic regression model with precision, recall, and AUC on the labelled sample; a first draft of the teacher-facing report template. |
| Months 7–9 | The model is applied to the full 4,200-student dataset. The teacher report is iterated with feedback from the pilot school. A short technical paper is drafted. The company receives the model, the report template, and documentation sufficient to run it on future-year exports. | A deployable guessing-risk scoring pipeline; a finialised teacher report template; a submitted or ready-to-submit paper; project closed before the next school year. |

### First six months
- Month 1 — data transfer: the company exports anonymised CSVs for both school years and delivers them to the master's student under a signed data-use agreement; Mitrović's group sets up a secure analysis environment.
- Month 1–2 — feature definition: Mitrović and the company's pedagogy contact (one day per week) agree on the three to five behavioural features to extract and draft a teacher-labelling protocol for the pilot school.
- Month 2–3 — profile discovery: the master's student runs latent profile analysis and HMM fitting; Mitrović reviews the profiles and selects the best-fitting solution for presentation to the company.
- Month 4–5 — teacher labelling: the company's pedagogy contact coordinates with two or three pilot-school teachers to label a sample of students; the master's student trains and evaluates the logistic regression model on those labels.

### What each side brings
- **Company:** Anonymised clickstream event logs for 4,200 students across two school years, covering question ID, answer, timestamp, attempt count, and time-on-question, in CSV format. [C002-CH1, C002/job/2024-06-01/Freelance Data Analyst — Learning Outcomes Project (Short-Term Contract)] Ongoing relationships with classroom teachers in Zrenjanin and surrounding municipalities, enabling teacher labelling and pilot testing. [C002/website/2024-02-10/What We Do — Zrenjanin Game Works] A company pedagogy contact is available for pedagogy input on approximately one day per week. [C002]
- **Faculty:** Mitrović co-authored sequence clustering of engagement trajectories using dynamic time warping and k-medoids. [SYN-PUB-10455] Mitrović co-authored student performance prediction from clickstream data, identifying quiz-attempt features as most portable across courses. [SYN-PUB-10457] Mitrović completed a four-month consultancy with an e-learning content provider advising on learner progress scoring systems, bringing experience translating analytic models into platform-usable outputs. [R1006]

### Why this pair
The company holds two years of clickstream logs from 4,200 students and has teacher relationships that can supply ground-truth labels, but has no method to construct behavioural profiles from those logs or build a validated flag model. Mitrović brings latent variable modelling of clickstream sequences, trajectory clustering, and portable quiz-attempt prediction, along with prior experience advising on the design of a learner progress scoring system for an e-learning platform. Neither could do this alone: the company brings the data, the domain context, and the teacher access needed to label and pilot the output; Mitrović's group brings the methods and the analytical capacity to build, validate, and document a model the company can operate year on year.

- The company has two school years of clickstream logs for 4,200 students and no analytical method to distinguish guessing from learning in those logs. [C002-CH1]
- Mitrović co-authored HMM modelling of clickstream sequences and co-authored longitudinal latent profile analysis of student learning data, as well as sequence clustering of engagement trajectories. [SYN-PUB-10456, SYN-PUB-10459, SYN-PUB-10455]
- Mitrović co-authored prediction work showing quiz-attempt features are the most portable clickstream features across courses. [SYN-PUB-10457]

### Risks and constraints
- The records do not include work on guessing or disengaged-responding detection specifically; the clustering and prediction work covers dropout and performance, which is a related but distinct outcome from random-click detection. [SYN-PUB-10454, SYN-PUB-10455, SYN-PUB-10457]
- The output must be explainable and actionable for classroom teachers without statistical training (C002/job/2024-06-01); the researcher's prediction work uses gradient-boosted trees and LSTM neural networks (SYN-PUB-10457, SYN-PUB-10458). proposals.title: Unsupervised Autoencoder Baseline Learning for On-Device ICS Protocol Anomaly Detection
proposals.markdown:
## Unsupervised Autoencoder Baseline Learning for On-Device ICS Protocol Anomaly Detection

**Company:** ArmaturaSec d.o.o. works in cybersecurity. [C001] Challenge C001-CH1.  
**Researcher:** Vuk Đukić is an Associate Professor in the Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences. [R1015]  
**Format:** joint project, one page.

### The problem
ArmaturaSec has collected several terabytes of Modbus and BACnet traffic captures from consenting client sites over three years, but no confirmed malicious traffic examples exist. [C001-CH1] Supervised classifiers trained on public ICS datasets produced unacceptable false positive rates in real deployments and were switched off by clients. [C001-CH1, C001/blog/2024-05-20/Why We Stopped Trying to Use Public ICS Datasets for Anomaly Detection] ArmaturaSec intends to release a hardware variant with a dedicated security processor to support on-device anomaly detection without affecting packet forwarding latency. [C001] Anomaly alerts must be explainable in plain language to plant managers. [C001-CH1]

### Prior work
- A 2024 study reports that a composite autoencoder model detects anomalous behaviour in ICS network traffic without pre-labelled data, using the HAI benchmark dataset. [W4391996970]
- A 2023 study reports an isolation-forest anomaly detection model that trains on an ESP32 microcontroller in 1.2 to 6.4 seconds and detects anomalies in under 16 milliseconds using 80 KB of RAM. [W4321372735]

### Research questions
1. Can an autoencoder trained solely on normal Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP traffic from a single client site detect behavioural deviations with a false positive rate low enough that plant managers do not disable alerts? Measured as alerts-per-clean-week on three held-out site captures from the company's archives.
2. Can the trained model be compressed and deployed on the ProtoSense hardware without adding measurable latency to packet forwarding? Measured as per-packet inference time and forwarding delay before and after model deployment on the target device.
3. Do reconstruction-error explanations expressed as protocol-field deltas communicate the anomaly cause clearly enough for plant managers to decide on a response? Measured by structured feedback from at least five plant-manager interviews conducted during the field trial.

### Approach
- Extract per-session and per-message features from the company's Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP captures, then train a site-specific autoencoder — using the autoencoder architecture from the researcher's published ICS anomaly detection work — on normal traffic only, with no labelled attack examples.
- Apply the model compression and quantisation techniques from the researcher's work on intrusion detection for resource-constrained IoT devices to reduce model footprint and inference time, targeting deployment on the ProtoSense embedded Linux environment without touching the packet-forwarding path.
- Generate reconstruction-error explanations at the protocol-field level (function code, register address, value range) so that each alert names the specific field that deviated; validate that plant managers can interpret these explanations through structured interviews during the field trial.
- Run a sliding-window recalibration procedure on held-out normal traffic to set alert thresholds per site, avoiding any reliance on public ICS attack datasets.

### Plan

| Period | Work | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Months 1–3 | Transfer a representative subset of the company's Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP captures (under NDA) to the researcher's lab. A master's student, supervised by Vuk Đukić, preprocesses the captures and extracts protocol-level features. The company engineer reviews feature definitions against the firmware's protocol parser. | A labelled feature dataset from at least three client sites, ready for model training; a short data-quality report. |
| Months 4–6 | Train and tune the autoencoder baseline model on site-specific normal traffic. Apply model compression to meet the on-device memory and latency target. Implement per-field reconstruction-error explanations and test them with internal reviewers at the company. | A compressed model that passes a latency benchmark on the ProtoSense hardware; a prototype explanation interface; a draft technical report on false-positive rates across the three held-out site captures. |
| Months 7–9 | Deploy the detector on the ProtoSense module at one consenting client site. Collect field observations, gather structured plant-manager feedback on explanation clarity, and adjust threshold calibration based on live normal traffic. | A field-trial report with false positive counts, latency measurements, and plant-manager feedback scores; a decision on whether threshold recalibration is sufficient or a concept-drift mechanism is needed. |
| Months 10–12 | Integrate accepted findings into the firmware codebase. Finalise documentation for the company. Prepare a joint conference or journal paper covering the on-device unsupervised detection method and the field-trial results. | Production-ready detector integrated in the ProtoSense firmware; one submitted joint publication. |

### First six months
- Week 1–2: Company and researcher sign NDA and data-transfer agreement; company engineer identifies which site captures are cleared for transfer and prepares anonymised copies.
- Week 3–6: Master's student from the researcher's group sets up a parsing pipeline for Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP pcap files, cross-checked against the company's firmware protocol parser, and produces a first feature matrix.
- Month 2–3: Vuk Đukić and the master's student train a first autoencoder on one site's normal traffic, measure reconstruction-error distributions, and report a baseline false positive rate to the company engineer.
- Month 4–6: Apply compression and quantisation to the trained model; benchmark inference time on a ProtoSense hardware unit supplied by the company; deliver a go/no-go report on on-device feasibility before the field trial.

### What each side brings
- **Company:** Several terabytes of normal Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP traffic captures from consenting client sites collected over three years. [C001-CH1, C001, C001/job/2024-02-05/Firmware Engineer — Network Protocols (Zrenjanin)] ProtoSense hardware and an embedded Linux firmware codebase with protocol parsing and access control components for integration and benchmarking. [C001-CH1, C001, C001/job/2024-02-05/Firmware Engineer — Network Protocols (Zrenjanin)] The company has one engineer who has been reading about anomaly detection for six months, and can dedicate one to two engineers part-time to a collaborative project. [C001-CH1, C001]
- **Faculty:** Vuk Đukić co-authored work on unsupervised anomaly detection on industrial control system protocols using autoencoder-based neural networks. [SYN-PUB-10523] Vuk Đukić co-authored work on intrusion detection on resource-constrained IoT devices using compressed recurrent neural network models. [SYN-PUB-10531] Vuk Đukić led the academic partner contribution to SECURE-ICS, an Innovation Fund project developing security monitoring for factory automation systems on Modbus, PROFINET, and EtherNet/IP protocols. [SYN-PRJ-0017]

### Why this pair
The company holds years of real operational traffic but has no anomaly detection method that works without labelled attacks. Vuk Đukić brings the two exact capabilities the problem needs — autoencoder-based unsupervised detection on ICS protocols and model compression for resource-constrained devices — developed in peer-reviewed work. Neither side can do it alone: the company brings the only asset that makes per-site baseline learning possible (large-scale real traffic from live installations), while the researcher brings the methods and a master's student to apply them within a realistic project timeline.

- ArmaturaSec has several terabytes of real Modbus and BACnet traffic from consenting client sites and no confirmed attack labels; supervised classifiers trained on public datasets produced unacceptable false positive rates and were switched off by clients. [C001-CH1, C001/blog/2024-05-20/Why We Stopped Trying to Use Public ICS Datasets for Anomaly Detection]
- Vuk Đukić co-authored work on autoencoder-based unsupervised anomaly detection on ICS protocols and co-authored work on compressed RNN models for resource-constrained IoT intrusion detection. [SYN-PUB-10523, SYN-PUB-10531]
- Vuk Đukić led the academic partner contribution to SECURE-ICS, an Innovation Fund project developing security monitoring for factory automation systems on Modbus, PROFINET, and EtherNet/IP protocols. [SYN-PRJ-0017]

### Risks and constraints
- The published record covers autoencoder-based detection on ICS protocols (SYN-PUB-10523) but does not evidence threshold calibration or sliding-window recalibration on unlabelled operational data specifically. [SYN-PUB-10523, C001-CH1]
- Vuk Đukić co-authored work on intrusion detection on resource-constrained IoT devices using compressed recurrent neural network models; ArmaturaSec intends to release a hardware variant with a dedicated security processor to support on-device anomaly detection without affecting packet forwarding latency. [SYN-PUB-10531, C001]

### Agreed up front (proposed)
- Publication: either party may submit a joint paper after a 45-day written review by the company; the company may request redaction of client-identifying site details before submission.
- Ownership: the company owns the trained models, the compressed firmware component, and any code integrated into ProtoSense; the researcher's group retains the underlying methods and may reuse them in future academic work.
- Data access: all traffic captures are transferred under a signed NDA and stored only on university systems approved by the company; copies are deleted at project end unless both parties agree otherwise.
- Preconditions: client consents for data use in research must be confirmed in writing before transfer; the company confirms that no personal data under GDPR or the Serbian Personal Data Protection Act is present in the captures, or provides a data-protection impact assessment before transfer begins.

### Sources

- C001-CH1: We need to detect unusual behaviour on Modbus and BACnet networks without labelled attack data — our clients have nev...

proposals.title: Thermo-Mechanical Fatigue Characterisation of Weld Joints in Cold-Store Conveyor Frames
proposals.markdown:
## Thermo-Mechanical Fatigue Characterisation of Weld Joints in Cold-Store Conveyor Frames

**Company:** AutomVoj a.d. works in robotics and industrial automation. [C003] Challenge C003-CH1.  
**Researcher:** Bojan Erić is an Associate Professor in the Department of Mechanical Engineering (Machine Design and Mechanics), Faculty of Technical Sciences. [R0365]  
**Format:** joint project, one page.

### The problem
Mild steel conveyor frames crack at crossmember-to-stringer weld joints after roughly 18 months of continuous operation in food-processing cold stores at 2–6 °C, and AutomVoj has replaced 14 assemblies under warranty this year. [C003-CH1] The company has tested frames under load at room temperature and cannot reproduce the failure, and suspects that thermal cycling, condensation, and vibration interact to cause the cracking. [C003-CH1] The company has photographs, measurements from site visits, and two failed frame sections with visible weld cracks available for investigation. [C003-CH1]

### Prior work
- A 2024 study reports that the crack growth rate of welded steel joints in a corrosive environment is higher than that of base metal, driven by residual stress and high dislocation density in the heat-affected zone. [W4402945203]

### Research questions
1. Does the crossmember-to-stringer weld joint in mild steel conveyor frames initiate cracks under combined low-temperature thermal cycling (2–6 °C operating range) and cyclic mechanical loading at frequencies representative of conveyor vibration? Measured by crack initiation life and crack opening displacement on specimens machined from the company's failed frames and from newly fabricated reference joints, tested in the climate chamber at low temperature.
2. Does residual stress in the weld toe — measured by X-ray diffraction and hole-drilling on the failed sections and modelled by finite element simulation with kinematic hardening — concentrate stress intensity to a level that explains the observed 18-month crack initiation period? Measured against fracture mechanics thresholds computed using XFEM for the joint geometry.
3. Can a change to welding procedure, filler material, or joint geometry reduce the weld-toe stress intensity factor by a measurable margin under the same combined loading conditions? Measured by comparing crack initiation life and residual stress level between the current joint and candidate improved joints in climate-chamber tests.

### Approach
- Fractographic and metallographic analysis of the two failed frame sections: map crack morphology, identify initiation sites at the weld toe or root, and characterise HAZ microstructure using Charpy and CTOD sub-size specimens at sub-zero temperature, following the method used in Erić's fracture-toughness characterisation of HAZ at sub-zero temperatures.
- Residual stress measurement on the failed sections and on reference weld joints fabricated to the company's current welding procedure: hole-drilling for through-thickness profile and X-ray diffraction for surface stress; finite element simulation with kinematic hardening models residual stress redistribution under cyclic loading, following the methods in Erić's published work on residual stress in welded joints.
- Combined thermo-mechanical fatigue testing on weld-joint specimens in the climate chamber: thermal cycling across the cold-store operating range, with simultaneous cyclic mechanical loading representative of conveyor vibration amplitude; digital image correlation monitors crack closure and full-field strain at the weld toe, following the experimental protocol from Erić's thermo-mechanical fatigue studies.
- XFEM computation of stress intensity factors at the weld toe for the current joint geometry and for candidate improved geometries; results from the residual stress measurements are used as initial conditions; candidates showing a reduced stress intensity factor are fabricated to the company's welding capability and re-tested in the climate chamber.

### Plan

| Period | Work | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Months 1–3 | Transfer the two failed frame sections to the faculty laboratory. A master's student, supervised by Erić, performs fractographic analysis, metallographic sectioning, and sub-zero Charpy and CTOD testing on HAZ specimens. The company's engineer provides welding procedure records, filler material specification, and site vibration measurements. Residual stress is measured on the failed sections by hole-drilling and X-ray diffraction. | Failure origin identified (weld toe or root, HAZ or fusion line); as-found residual stress map; sub-zero fracture toughness values for the HAZ microstructure. Go/no-go decision on whether condensation-assisted corrosion needs a separate test stream. |
| Months 4–6 | Fabricate reference weld joints to the company's current procedure. Run combined thermo-mechanical fatigue tests in the climate chamber: thermal cycling across the cold-store range, cyclic mechanical load at the measured vibration amplitude. Digital image correlation monitors crack closure and strain at the weld toe. Finite element model with kinematic hardening is calibrated against the measured residual stress data. | Reproduced crack initiation under low-temperature combined loading; calibrated FE model; stress intensity factor history at the weld toe. Dataset of test records and DIC images available to both parties. |
| Months 7–9 | XFEM analysis of the current and candidate improved joint geometries (modified toe geometry, alternative filler, post-weld heat treatment) using measured residual stress as initial conditions. Fabricate two or three candidate joints to the company's fabrication capability and run climate-chamber fatigue tests. Compare crack initiation life and residual stress against the baseline. | Ranked shortlist of welding procedure or joint design changes with quantified improvement in crack initiation life. Final report with implementation-ready recommendations and a draft technical paper. |

### First six months
- Week 1–2: AutomVoj ships the two failed frame sections and transfers welding procedure records, filler material data sheets, and vibration amplitude measurements from site visits to the faculty laboratory.
- Week 3–6: Erić's master's student carries out fractographic and metallographic examination and machines sub-zero Charpy and CTOD specimens from the HAZ of the failed sections;
- Month 2: Hole-drilling and X-ray diffraction residual stress measurements on the failed sections, carried out in the faculty laboratory by the master's student; Erić reviews and interprets results.
- Month 3: Climate chamber and servo-hydraulic machine time is booked (advance coordination required); reference weld joints are fabricated by the company to the current procedure and shipped to the faculty for combined thermo-mechanical fatigue testing starting in month 4.

### What each side brings
- **Company:** Two failed frame sections are held in storage, and the company has photographs and measurements of the cracked joints from site visits. [C003-CH1] In-house fabrication shop with mild steel and stainless steel MIG/MAG welding capability. [C003] Photographs and measurements of cracked joints collected during site visits to cold-store installations operating at 2–6 °C. [C003-CH1]
- **Faculty:** Erić co-authored studies on thermo-mechanical fatigue of butt-welded structures under combined cyclic mechanical loading and thermal cycling between −30 °C and +20 °C, including digital image correlation of crack closure at the weld. [SYN-PUB-04475, SYN-PUB-04482] Erić co-authored work on fracture toughness characterisation of HAZ microstructures in high-strength steels at sub-zero temperatures using Charpy and CTOD testing. [SYN-PUB-04476] Erić co-authored work on residual stress measurement in welded joints by hole-drilling and X-ray diffraction, and on finite element modelling of residual stress relaxation under cyclic loading. [SYN-PUB-04473, SYN-PUB-04478] Erić co-authored work on XFEM computation of stress intensity factors at weld-toe cracks under combined loading in Abaqus, and can access a servo-hydraulic fatigue testing machine and a climate chamber capable of reaching −60 °C. [SYN-PUB-04477, R0365]

### Why this pair
AutomVoj has the failed hardware, the fabrication capability, and the operational context, but lacks low-temperature fatigue testing equipment and the fracture mechanics methods needed to reproduce and diagnose the failure. Erić's group has the climate chamber, servo-hydraulic machine, digital image correlation setup, and a published track record of exactly the combined thermo-mechanical fatigue and residual stress work the diagnosis requires — Together they cover every element of the investigation: neither side could reproduce the failure, characterise its mechanism, and produce implementable design recommendations without the other.

- AutomVoj cannot reproduce the failure at room temperature; testing must occur at low temperature under thermal cycling, which requires equipment the company does not have. [C003-CH1]
- Erić co-authored studies of thermo-mechanical fatigue in welded structures under thermal cycling between −30 °C and +20 °C and has access to a climate chamber reaching −60 °C and a servo-hydraulic fatigue machine. [SYN-PUB-04475, SYN-PUB-04482, R0365]
- Erić co-authored work on residual stress measurement in welded joints and XFEM fracture mechanics analysis of weld-toe cracks under combined loading. [SYN-PUB-04473, SYN-PUB-04478, SYN-PUB-04477]

### Risks and constraints
- The climate chamber and servo-hydraulic machines are shared equipment and require advance coordination for extended campaigns (R0365). [R0365]
- The records cover fatigue and fracture under mechanical and thermal cycling; the corrosion-assisted component from condensation is not addressed in the published work. [SYN-PUB-04482, SYN-PUB-04475, SYN-PUB-04474]

### Agreed up front (proposed)
- Publication: results may be submitted for publication after a 60-day written review period by AutomVoj; the company may request redaction of specific proprietary weld procedure details.
- Ownership: AutomVoj owns the test data, the calibrated finite element model, and any recommendations for welding procedure or joint design changes; the Faculty of Technical Sciences retains the right to use the experimental methods and general findings in future academic work.
- Data access: AutomVoj transfers the two failed frame sections, welding procedure records, filler material data sheets, and site vibration measurements to the faculty laboratory within two weeks of project start; data is handled under a signed confidentiality agreement.
- Preconditions: the climate chamber and servo-hydraulic machine must be booked at least four weeks in advance; the project start date is contingent on confirmed equipment availability for months 4–6.

### Sources

- C003-CH1: Our conveyor frames crack at the weld joints after roughly 18 months of operation in chilled environments; we've repl...
- R0365: Bojan Erić
- SYN-PUB-04473: Effect of Post-Weld Heat Treatment on Residual Stress Distribution in T-Joint Welds of Low-Alloy Steel (2012)
- SYN-PUB-04474: Low-Cycle Fatigue Behaviour of Cruciform Welded Joints at −40 °C: An Experimental Study (2014)
- SYN-PUB-04475: Interaction of Mechanical Cyclic Loading and Thermal Cycling on Fatigue Life of Butt-Welded Structural Steel Plates (2016)
- SYN-PUB-04476: Fracture Toughness of Heat-Affected Zone Microstructures in S690QL High-Strength Steel Welds at Sub-Zero Temperatures (2017)
- SYN-PUB-04477: Finite-Element Estimation of Stress Intensity Factors for Surface Cracks at Weld Toes Under Combined Bending and Torsion (2018)
- SYN-PUB-04478: Weld Residual Stress Relaxation Under Cyclic Loading: Measurements and Modelling for S355 Cruciform Joints (2019)

proposals.title: Synthetic Augmentation and Cross-Lingual Transfer for Serbian Court-Decision Outcome Prediction
proposals.markdown:
## Synthetic Augmentation and Cross-Lingual Transfer for Serbian Court-Decision Outcome Prediction

**Company:** PravniPilot a.d. works in legal tech. [C006] Challenge C006-CH1.  
**Researcher:** Jovan Puzović is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences. [R0484]  
**Format:** joint project, one page.

### The problem
A case-outcome prediction model trained on roughly 9,000 labeled Serbian commercial-dispute decisions achieves 61% accuracy and has plateaued near 63% despite basic data augmentation and fine-tuned multilingual pre-trained models. [C006-CH1] The company estimates it needs at least 40,000 clean labeled decisions to reach the target 75% accuracy, but Serbian courts do not publish decisions in a consistent machine-readable format, making it hard to scale the labeled corpus without substantial manual effort. [C006-CH1] PravniPilot must reach 75% accuracy on a held-out test set within 12 months to market the prediction feature with honest confidence intervals. [C006-CH1]

### Prior work
- A 2025 study on low-resource Sindhi text classification reports that EDA, particularly Random Deletion, achieves 99% F1 for binary classification on 3,364 news articles using a fine-tuned multilingual BERT model, while back-translation and paraphrasing also deliver substantial improvements. [W4411347520]
- A 2021 systematic comparison reports that text augmentation at the token and syntax levels improves sequence tagging for low-resource languages when combined with pretrained multilingual contextualized models such as mBERT, with gains most pronounced on morphologically rich languages. [W3214193653]

### Research questions
1. Can synthetic legal text generation — using conditional language models and back-translation from Croatian and Bosnian decisions — combined with cost-sensitive fine-tuning lift case-outcome prediction accuracy from 63% to at least 75% on the held-out Serbian commercial-dispute test set, measured by macro-averaged accuracy and F1 on that fixed set?
2. Which combination of cross-lingual transfer source (Croatian only, Bosnian only, both) and intermediate pretraining strategy produces the largest accuracy gain on the Serbian test set, measured by ablation on the same held-out set?
3. Does a semi-supervised labeling step applied to unlabeled decisions in the two-million-decision corpus increase accuracy further, measured by comparing the fully supervised and semi-supervised models on the held-out test set?

### Approach
- Extract and align Croatian and Bosnian decisions from the existing corpus using the company's PDF/HTML parser and annotation tool; apply Puzović's intermediate pretraining strategy — domain-adaptive pretraining on unlabeled Serbian, Croatian and Bosnian legal text — to adapt a multilingual transformer before fine-tuning on the 9,000 labeled Serbian decisions.
- Apply Puzović's synthetic legal text generation pipeline — conditional language-model generation and back-translation — to the labeled Serbian corpus to produce additional training examples; validate synthetic-data quality against the company's annotators using the domain-expertise evaluation protocol from prior work.
- Fine-tune the augmented model with cost-sensitive learning objectives (focal loss, weighted cross-entropy) from Puzović's imbalanced-classification work to address any class skew in case outcomes, targeting the 75% accuracy threshold on the held-out test set.
- Package the trained model and inference pipeline as a Python/PyTorch module with a PostgreSQL-compatible serving wrapper, integrable directly into the production codebase, and run a final ablation to report each component's contribution.

### Plan

| Period | Work | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Months 1–3 | Set up a shared data pipeline. Use the company's parser and annotation tool to extract and clean Serbian, Croatian and Bosnian decisions from the corpus. Define a fixed held-out test set. Run intermediate pretraining on unlabeled text from all three jurisdictions. A master's student from Puzović's group does day-to-day work; the company's data engineer handles parser integration and annotators confirm label quality. | A clean multi-jurisdiction pretraining corpus; a fixed held-out test set; a domain-pretrained multilingual transformer; a baseline accuracy figure on the held-out set. |
| Months 4–6 | Run the synthetic text generation and back-translation pipeline on the labeled Serbian training set. Validate synthetic examples with the company's annotators. Fine-tune the pretrained model on the expanded labeled set. Test augmentation variants (generation only, back-translation only, combined). The master's student runs experiments; the company's two data scientists review outputs at roughly two days per week. | An augmented training corpus; fine-tuned model variants; accuracy and F1 scores per augmentation strategy on the held-out set; a draft technical report. |
| Months 7–9 | Apply semi-supervised labeling to a sample of unlabeled decisions from the corpus using the best model so far. Re-train with cost-sensitive objectives. Puzović guides the semi-supervised design; the company's data engineer integrates new labels into the annotation tool; the master's student runs the full ablation grid. | A semi-supervised extended labeled set; ablation table showing each component's contribution; updated accuracy on the held-out set. |
| Months 10–12 | Package the final model as a Python/PyTorch inference module with a PostgreSQL-compatible wrapper. Run integration tests in the company's staging environment. Write a joint paper. The company's engineers lead integration; the master's student and Puzović finalize the paper. | A production-ready model and serving module integrated into the company's codebase; final accuracy on the held-out test set reported against the 75% target; a submitted joint paper. |

### First six months
- Week 1–2: The company's data engineer shares a sample of 500 Serbian, Croatian and Bosnian decisions with the researcher's group under a signed data-access agreement; the two sides agree on the fixed held-out test-set composition and label schema.
- Month 1: The master's student installs the pretraining pipeline on the company's PyTorch stack using the company's corpus index; the data engineer validates the parser output for Croatian and Bosnian formats.
- Month 2: Intermediate pretraining runs on the unlabeled multi-jurisdiction text; the master's student reports a baseline fine-tuned accuracy on the held-out test set to confirm the 63% starting point.
- Month 3: Synthetic text generation and back-translation pipeline is set up; the company's annotators evaluate the first batch of synthetic examples for legal plausibility; go/no-go decision on each augmentation strategy before month 4.

### What each side brings
- **Company:** A corpus of over two million published court decisions across Serbia, Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, currently indexed and searchable. [C006] An internal annotation tool for labeling case outcomes and a custom PDF and HTML parser for court-document ingestion. [C006] One full-time data engineer and two part-time annotators for data cleaning and labeling, and a development team that can allocate roughly two days per week to collaborative research work. [C006, C006-CH1] PyTorch for transformer-based text classification and access to pre-trained multilingual transformer models. [C006, C006-CH1]
- **Faculty:** Puzović co-authored work on synthetic legal text generation using conditional language models and back-translation for data augmentation, and evaluated synthetic data validity against domain expertise. [SYN-PUB-05711, SYN-PUB-05710, SYN-PUB-05707] Puzović co-authored work on classification of imbalanced legal text datasets using resampling strategies and cost-sensitive learning objectives. [SYN-PUB-05712, SYN-PUB-03940, SYN-PUB-05706] Puzović co-authored work on transfer learning and intermediate pretraining strategies for adapting general language models to specialised legal domains on small datasets. [SYN-PUB-05708, SYN-PRJ-0554] Puzović led a project covering corpus construction and annotation guidelines for outcome and procedural-stage labels in Serbian legal text, and co-authored work on named entity recognition for domain-specific Serbian text. [SYN-PRJ-0554, SYN-PUB-05713]

### Why this pair
The company has a large, well-indexed corpus and the annotation infrastructure to scale labeling, but its in-house team has exhausted standard fine-tuning approaches and cannot independently design synthetic generation or cross-lingual pretraining pipelines for a low-resource South Slavic legal setting. Puzović brings exactly the methods the problem needs — synthetic legal text generation, cost-sensitive imbalanced classification, and domain-adaptive pretraining on small legal corpora — but would have no access to a two-million-decision proprietary corpus or to domain annotators able to validate synthetic legal output. Together they can close the data gap that neither side can close alone.

- The company's prediction model has plateaued at 63% on roughly 9,000 labeled Serbian commercial-dispute decisions, and the company needs to reach 75% within 12 months. [C006-CH1]
- Puzović co-authored work on synthetic legal text generation using conditional language models and back-translation for data augmentation, and evaluated synthetic data validity against domain expertise. [SYN-PUB-05711, SYN-PUB-05710, SYN-PUB-05707]
- The company holds a corpus of over two million published court decisions across Serbia, Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, currently indexed and searchable. [C006]

### Risks and constraints
- The published work covers legal text classification broadly; it is not confirmed to cover Serbian commercial-dispute court-decision formats specifically (SYN-PUB-05712, SYN-PUB-05708). [SYN-PUB-05712, SYN-PUB-05708]

### Agreed up front (proposed)
- Publication: results may be submitted for publication after a 30-day review by PravniPilot; the company may request redaction of proprietary details about the corpus or annotation schema, but may not block publication on scientific grounds.
- Ownership: PravniPilot owns the trained models, the augmented labeled dataset, and the production inference module; the University of Novi Sad retains the right to reuse the methods, pretraining code, and anonymised benchmark results in future research.
- Data access: the company provides the researcher's group with access to a defined subset of the corpus under a signed data-processing agreement; raw decision text does not leave the company's infrastructure; the researcher's group works via a secure API or on-site environment.
- Preconditions: the data-access and data-processing agreement must be signed before any corpus data is transferred or accessed; both sides confirm the held-out test-set composition and label schema in writing before month-1 experiments begin.

proposals.title: Kriging-with-External-Drift Parcel Rainfall Estimation to Calibrate Parametric Insurance Triggers
proposals.markdown:
## Kriging-with-External-Drift Parcel Rainfall Estimation to Calibrate Parametric Insurance Triggers

**Company:** OsiguroMi d.o.o. works in insurtech — embedded micro-insurance and parametric products. [C004] Challenge C004-CH1.  
**Researcher:** Žarko Pejić is a Research Associate in the Remote Sensing and GIS Group, BioSense Institute. [R0364]  
**Format:** joint project, one page.

### The problem
OsiguroMi's parametric payout trigger is based on the nearest official weather station, which can be up to 30 km from a farmer's parcel, and terrain variation means a drought signal at the station can coincide with local rain on the field, or vice versa. [C004-CH1] The company holds access to RHMZS data and three private agro-meteorological networks totalling about 140 measurement points, but these have not yet been fused into a spatially continuous parcel-level rainfall product. [C004-CH1, C004] The payout trigger is a fixed contractual threshold that cannot be replaced; the correction must come from more accurate spatial rainfall estimation at the parcel level. [C004-CH1]

### Prior work
- A 2022 study reports that optimized kriging of relative rainfall anomalies against long-term means produces 30-year, 250-metre monthly grids from 622 stations, with leave-one-out cross-validation R² of 0.78 over complex terrain. [W4213059839]
- A 2021 study reports that selecting and rank-transforming personal weather station observations before kriging improves spatial interpolation of high-intensity precipitation events at 1-, 3-, 6-, 12-, and 24-hour aggregations. [W3005806384]

### Research questions
1. Can kriging with external drift, blending OsiguroMi's ~140-station network with IMERG satellite estimates, produce parcel-scale daily rainfall grids with lower leave-one-out cross-validation error than the single nearest-station baseline? Measured by RMSE and bias against withheld stations across the covered region.
2. How much does the basis risk — the probability that a parcel experiences drought while the trigger station does not, or vice versa — decrease when the corrected spatial grid replaces the raw station reading as input to the fixed contractual threshold? Measured by burn analysis over the available historical record across a sample of cadastral parcels.
3. Does the downscaling model transfer to the expanded network geometry expected in Bulgaria and Romania, where the company plans to expand its agro line through regional cooperatives? Measured by cross-validation RMSE on a held-out subset of stations simulating lower network density.

### Approach
- Apply kriging with external drift using IMERG satellite precipitation as the external covariate and OsiguroMi's ~140-station gauge network as the primary observations, producing daily parcel-scale rainfall grids for the covered region — following the field-scale downscaling method Pejić co-authored.
- Perform bias correction of the satellite covariate against the gauge network using multi-source blending (ERA5, IMERG) as documented in Pejić's prior work, to remove systematic over- or under-estimation before the kriging step.
- Run burn analysis on the resulting historical parcel-level rainfall series, using the fixed contractual threshold unchanged, to quantify how basis risk changes relative to the nearest-station baseline — applying the insurance calibration method from Pejić's crop index insurance publications.
- Validate the spatial model through leave-one-out cross-validation on the gauge network and test transferability to lower-density configurations representative of the Bulgaria and Romania expansion.

### Plan

| Period | Work | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Months 1–2 | Žarko Pejić and OsiguroMi's internal researcher audit and harmonise the ~140-station time series (RHMZS + three private networks) in the company's PostgreSQL environment; define parcel sample for burn analysis; download and bias-correct IMERG covariate over the study domain. | A clean, merged gauge–satellite dataset ready for interpolation; agreed parcel sample list. |
| Months 3–5 | Pejić's group builds and cross-validates the kriging-with-external-drift model; OsiguroMi's engineers integrate the daily grid output into the existing Python loss-modelling pipeline; burn analysis runs on the full historical record. | A validated parcel-scale daily rainfall grid; basis-risk comparison report against the nearest-station baseline, both delivered to the company. |
| Months 6–7 | Sensitivity run using a thinned station subset mimicking Bulgaria/Romania network density; write-up of methods and results for publication; company reviews draft for proprietary data. | Transferability assessment for expansion markets; a joint paper submitted after the company's review period. |

### First six months
- Weeks 1–3: OsiguroMi's internal researcher exports historical station time series from PostgreSQL and shares them with Pejić under the signed data agreement; Pejić downloads the matching IMERG archive for the region.
- Weeks 4–6: Pejić's group runs quality control and bias correction on all four station sources and the satellite covariate; OsiguroMi's engineers flag any gaps or format inconsistencies.
- Months 2–3: Pejić fits the kriging-with-external-drift model on the merged dataset and delivers leave-one-out cross-validation results;
- Months 4–5: OsiguroMi's internal researcher connects the daily grid to the Python loss model; burn analysis runs with the fixed contractual threshold; basis-risk reduction is measured against the nearest-station baseline.

### What each side brings
- **Company:** Access to RHMZS data and three private agro-meteorological networks totalling about 140 measurement points across the region. [C004-CH1, C004] A Python environment for actuarial modelling and trigger calibration, and PostgreSQL databases with time series for historical losses. [C004] One internal researcher for data modelling and two senior engineers who can dedicate part of their capacity to joint projects. [C004]
- **Faculty:** Žarko Pejić co-authored a method for kriging with external drift that blends IMERG satellite estimates with gauge networks to produce field-scale rainfall grids. [SYN-PUB-04461] Pejić co-authored burn analysis and basis risk assessment for crop index insurance across cadastral municipalities and sample parcels. [SYN-PUB-04462, SYN-PUB-04014] Pejić co-authored ordinary kriging methods for monthly rainfall mapping and a Bayesian kriging approach for merging gauge and satellite precipitation data. [SYN-PUB-04460, SYN-PUB-04463] Pejić provided technical consultancy to an agricultural insurance intermediary in 2023 on spatial resolution requirements for parametric rainfall products. [R0364]

### Why this pair
OsiguroMi has the station network, the historical loss data, and a working insurance pipeline, but needs the spatial estimation method to correct basis risk without touching the contractual threshold. Pejić brings the specific combination of kriging-with-external-drift downscaling and crop index insurance calibration that the problem requires; the company brings the proprietary multi-network gauge data and the operational context that turns the model into a live product. Neither could do it alone: without the company's approximately 140-station gauge network the spatial interpolation model has no operational grounding in the region, and without the researcher's published downscaling and burn-analysis methods the company has no validated path from raw station data to corrected parcel-level triggers.

- OsiguroMi's payout trigger is based on official stations up to 30 km from a farmer's parcel, and the goal is to correct payout logic through more accurate spatial estimation without replacing the contractual threshold. [C004-CH1]
- Pejić co-authored a kriging-with-external-drift method blending IMERG satellite estimates with gauge networks to produce field-scale rainfall grids. [SYN-PUB-04461]

### Risks and constraints
- The publications on multi-source bias correction cover ERA5, IMERG, and TMPA; coverage of the specific private agro-meteorological networks OsiguroMi holds is not documented in the record. [SYN-PUB-04014, SYN-PUB-04464, SYN-PUB-04463]
- The company requires results applicable within six to nine months. [C004]

### Agreed up front (proposed)
- Publication: results may be published after a 30-day review by OsiguroMi; the company may request redaction of commercially sensitive network configurations or loss ratios before submission.
- Ownership: OsiguroMi owns the fitted model, trained parameters, and any operational grid product; BioSense Institute retains the underlying geostatistical methods and may reuse them in future research.
- Data access: OsiguroMi provides station time series under a signed data-sharing agreement before work begins; Pejić's group uses the data solely for this project and deletes copies on project close.
- Precondition: the data-sharing agreement covering all four station sources (RHMZS and three private networks) must be signed before the dataset audit in Month 1 can start.

### Sources

- R0364: Žarko Pejić
- SYN-PUB-04014: Constructing a 25-Year Field-Scale Rainfall Archive for Vojvodina and Its Application to Historical Burn Analysis of... (2026)
- SYN-PUB-04460: Comparison of IDW and Ordinary Kriging for Monthly Rainfall Interpolation in the Vojvodina Lowlands Using a Sparse St... (2013)
- SYN-PUB-04461: Kriging with External Drift Using IMERG Precipitation as a Covariate for Sub-Monthly Rainfall Mapping at 1 km Resolut... (2018)
- SYN-PUB-04462: Design of a Rainfall Deficit Index for Maize Insurance in the Vojvodina Region: Sensitivity to Spatial Resolution of... (2020)
- SYN-PUB-04463: Merging Gauge and Satellite Precipitation Data in a Flat Agricultural Region: A Bayesian Kriging Approach (2022)
- SYN-PUB-04464: Assessment of Three Bias-Correction Methods Applied to IMERG Over the Pannonian Basin Prior to Geostatistical Downsca... (2023)
- W3005806384: The use of personal weather station observations to improve precipitation estimation and interpolation (2021) https://openalex.org/W3005806384
- W4213059839: Optimizing Automated Kriging to Improve Spatial Interpolation of Monthly Rainfall over Complex Terrain (2022) https://openalex.org/W4213059839

needsHuman.markdown:
## RSM-guided pyrolysis optimisation to reach 70% fixed carbon on existing batch reactor

**Company:** Suncokret Eko d.o.o. works in cleantech — biomass and organic waste valorisation. [C007] Challenge C007-CH1.  
**Researcher:** Đorđe Vukelić is an Associate Professor in the Department of Applied and Engineering Chemistry, Faculty of Technology. [R0992]  
**Format:** joint project, one page.

### The problem
Suncokret Eko's batch pyrolysis of sunflower husks and maize cobs runs at 500–520°C, producing biochar with 55% fixed carbon at 28% mass yield. [C007-CH1] Customers in Germany and the Netherlands require 70% fixed carbon for soil-amendment certification; raising temperature to 650°C meets the threshold but drops mass yield below 20%. [C007-CH1] A mass yield below 20% requires 40% more feedstock per order, eliminating the price premium the certified product commands. [C007-CH1] Feedstock arrives from different suppliers with variable moisture and particle size, adding process variability the company has not yet quantified. [C007-CH3]

### Prior work
- A 2023 study reports an RSM model that predicts biochar yield from fixed carbon content, reaction temperature, and heating rate, developed on a Box-Behnken design across three biomass types. [W4319953064]

### Research questions
1. Can a response-surface model, fitted to controlled production trials on the existing reactor, identify temperature–residence-time conditions that raise fixed-carbon content to at least 70% while keeping mass yield commercially viable — measured as fixed carbon and proximate analysis on each trial run, compared against the current 55%-fixed-carbon, 28%-yield baseline?
2. How much of the run-to-run variation in fixed-carbon output is explained by feedstock moisture and particle size, and can a pre-treatment or process-adjustment rule reduce that variation — measured by the coefficient of variation in fixed carbon across runs grouped by feedstock batch?

### Approach
- Map the two-year batch log to extract recorded temperature profiles, residence times, feedstock moisture, particle size, and proximate analysis results; use these to fit a preliminary response-surface model (central composite design) of fixed carbon and mass yield as functions of temperature and residence time — following the RSM and central composite design methodology from the researcher's published optimisation work.
- Run thermogravimetric analysis on representative sunflower husk and maize cob samples from current supplier batches to determine pyrolysis kinetics and conversion ranges using isoconversional methods, establishing the activation energy profile that explains the fixed-carbon plateau and informing the temperature bounds for the trial design.
- Execute a set of controlled production trials on the existing reactor at RSM-guided temperature–residence-time combinations — staying within the reactor's 400–700°C operating range — recording proximate analysis after each run; fit and validate the response-surface model to locate conditions that reach 70% fixed carbon at the highest feasible mass yield.
- Characterise the best-performing biochar against European Biochar Certificate stable-carbon criteria using the lab's proximate and ultimate analysis capability, supplemented by BET surface area and FTIR analysis at the Faculty of Technology, to confirm certification readiness.

### Plan

| Period | Work | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Months 1–2 | Đorđe Vukelić and a master's student extract and clean the two-year batch log. TGA runs on current feedstock samples at the Faculty of Technology establish kinetics. The preliminary RSM design is built. A company engineer participates roughly one day per week to prepare samples and retrieve log data. | A cleaned dataset of historical runs; TGA-derived activation energy estimates for current feedstocks; a trial design matrix of 15–20 reactor runs. |
| Months 3–4 | Company staff run the designed trials on the existing reactor; Vukelić and the master's student conduct proximate analysis and, for selected runs, BET and FTIR at the Faculty. The response-surface model is fitted and validated against trial results. | A fitted RSM model with confidence intervals; identification of the temperature–residence-time window that maximises fixed carbon subject to the mass-yield constraint. |
| Months 5–6 | Company staff run three confirmation batches at the model-recommended conditions. The master's student performs full EBC-criteria characterisation. Operating instructions for the adjusted process are drafted, including a feedstock moisture and particle-size screening rule. | A verified operating protocol for the existing reactor; a characterisation report against EBC stable-carbon criteria; a joint technical report suitable for a peer-reviewed submission. |

### First six months
- Week 1–2: the company transfers the two-year batch log (temperature profiles, feedstock metadata, proximate analysis records) to the Faculty of Technology under a signed data-sharing agreement; Vukelić and a master's student audit completeness and flag missing fields.
- Week 3–6: the master's student runs TGA-DSC analysis on at least three current feedstock samples (sunflower husk and maize cob from different supplier batches) at the Faculty lab to characterise kinetics and moisture sensitivity.
- Week 7–8: Vukelić delivers a trial design matrix (central composite or Box-Behnken) specifying the temperature and residence-time combinations to be tested, confirmed against the reactor's 400–700°C operating range and the company's batch schedule.
- Week 9 onward: a company engineer begins running designed trials one or two per week, recording all process parameters; the master's student visits for sample collection and proximate analysis after each run.

### What each side brings
- **Company:** A batch slow-pyrolysis reactor with a 400–700°C operating range, two years of production logs covering temperature profiles, feedstock moisture, particle size, and output quality. [C007, C007-CH1] Two technically trained staff who can run controlled production trials and maintain detailed process logs, available for trial execution throughout the project. [C007] In-house proximate and ultimate analysis capability for biochar (fixed carbon, ash, volatile matter). [C007] Baseline performance data: 28% mass yield and 55% fixed carbon at 500–520°C. [C007-CH1]
- **Faculty:** Đorđe Vukelić co-authored work on temperature–residence-time optimisation for biochar production using response surface methodology and central composite design. [SYN-PUB-10356] Vukelić holds a granted patent on a process for producing certified-grade biochar from sunflower husk by controlled slow pyrolysis with integrated temperature–residence-time feedback. [SYN-PAT-033] Vukelić co-authored work on physicochemical certification of biochar against European Biochar Certificate criteria including stable carbon content. [SYN-PUB-10349] The Faculty of Technology lab provides a TGA-DSC coupled analyser, a fixed-bed tube furnace reactor to 1100°C, BET surface area apparatus, and FTIR and Raman spectrometers for kinetic and characterisation work. [R0992]

### Why this pair
The company has two years of batch data and a working reactor but lacks the statistical and thermochemical methods to extract an optimal operating window from that data. Vukelić brings exactly the two methods the problem needs — response surface optimisation of the temperature–residence-time space and EBC certification characterisation — and holds a patent on the specific feedstock. Neither could do it alone: the company provides the reactor, the production trials, and the batch log that the model must be fitted to; the researcher provides the kinetic analysis, the RSM design, the characterisation lab, and a student to do the day-to-day analytical work.

- Suncokret Eko has two years of batch logs and an existing reactor but needs a method to map temperature–residence-time conditions to fixed-carbon yield without capital investment. [C007-CH1, C007]
- Vukelić co-authored published work on RSM optimisation of biochar temperature–residence-time conditions and holds a patent on certified-grade biochar production from sunflower husk. [SYN-PUB-10356, SYN-PAT-033]
- Vukelić co-authored work on EBC physicochemical certification including stable carbon content, directly matching the 70% fixed-carbon certification target. [SYN-PUB-10349]

### Risks and constraints
- The company requires a process adjustment testable within six months, involving controlled production trials on the existing reactor. [C007-CH1]

### Agreed up front (proposed)
- Publication: the company has 45 days to review any manuscript before submission; results from the controlled production trials may be published after that review period.
- Ownership: the company owns the validated operating protocol and any process adjustments derived from the trials; the Faculty of Technology retains the right to use the kinetic data and RSM model for further research and teaching.
- Data access: the company provides the two-year batch log to the Faculty under a signed confidentiality agreement; the Faculty uses it solely for this project and deletes or returns it on completion.
